newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-CRACKED PITCH CAUSES AUSTRALIA CONCERN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CRACKED PITCH CAUSES AUSTRALIA CONCERN.

text.p: Australia are considering a three-pronged spin attack for the one-off test against India beginning on Thursday after seeing the deteriorating state of the pitch at New Delhi's Feroz Shah Kotla stadium.
Left-arm spinner Brad Hogg and leg-spinner Peter McIntyre have been included in the squad of 12, and Australia will have a third option in part-time off-spinner Mark Waugh.
"Spinners will get plenty of help from this track and we are considering the possibility of playing an extra spin bowler," Australian skipper Mark Taylor said after practice on Wednesday.
Waugh turned his off-breaks to take six for 68 in the second innings of Australia's warm-up match against the Indian Board President's XI that ended in a draw on Monday.
Damien Fleming and Stuart Law have been left out of the 12 and there is likely to be a final choice between Hogg and medium pacer Jason Gillespie.
Taylor expressed concern about the pitch lasting the full match, to be played for the newly-instituted Border-Gavaskar Trophy honouring the two batsmen to have scored over 10,000 runs in tests.
"This is the driest wicket I've seen even on the sub-continent," Taylor said.
"Winning the toss on this pitch will be a big advantage and I hope the pitch lasts five days."
Indian captain Sachin Tendulkar, worried by the sore shoulder of medium pacer Javagal Srinath who has missed practice for the last two days, agreed with Taylor's assessment of the pitch.
"The wicket is extremely dry and I too will elect to bat if I win the toss," Tendulkar said.
"Switching from one-dayers to tests is not easy," he said, emphasising the surfeit of one-day internationals in India's international engagements.
India, who have the luxury of picking from four spinners, will extend the one-day experiment of opening the innings with wicketkeeper-batsman Nayan Mongia.
India's new coach Madan Lal said they were awaiting news on Srinath's condition before naming their 12.

This will be the 51st test between India and Australia. Australia have won 24 and India eight. Seventeen of these failed to produce a result and one, during the last series in India in 1986, was tied.

India (from) - Vikram Rathore, Nayan Mongia, Saurav Ganguly, Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Sunil Joshi, Vangipurappu Laxman, Aashish Kapoor, Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, Venkatesh Prasad, Narendra Hirwani, David Johnson.
Australia (from) - Mark Taylor (captain), Michael Slater, Ricky Ponting, Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Brad Hogg, Jason Gillespie, Peter McIntyre, Paul Reiffel and Glen McGrath.
